Two other services covering your area, **LINK Paratransit** and **One-Seat Regional Ride**, are ruled out for you — both require a disability certification you don't have.

turns.user: I need a ride from Richmond City Hall to Kaiser Permanente Richmond Medical Center on August 12, 2026, departing at noon, round trip returning at 3:00 PM. I'm 68, I live in Richmond, I'm not disabled, not ADA-certified, and not a veteran.
turns.message:
Good news — you qualify for two door-to-door options for your round trip on Wednesday, August 12.

**R-Transit (Richmond)** — city paratransit for Richmond residents 55+. $3.00 each way, paid by ticket. Book at least 7 days ahead: **(510) 307-8026**. First-time riders need to complete an R-Transit application with photo ID and a piece of mail showing your Richmond address.

**Mobility Matters** — free volunteer driver program for Contra Costa residents 60+. Also 7 days advance notice: **(925) 284-6161**. They describe themselves as a last-resort option, so availability depends on a volunteer being free.

Two things to know:
- Neither provider's operating hours are in our records, so please confirm the noon pickup and 3:00 PM return when you call — I can't guarantee those times.
- To make the 7-day notice, call by **Wednesday, August 5**. Sooner is better, especially for Mobility Matters.

East Bay Paratransit also serves this route but requires ADA certification, so it's not an option for you.

One more thing: it's only about a mile — roughly a 24-minute walk — from City Hall to the medical center, if that's ever useful.

OPTIMAT doesn't book rides, so you'll need to call the provider directly. Want details on either one?
